title: Blood Resonance
next_chapter_hook: The phantom was about to dissipate when his father's aged voice echoed through the empty ruins: 'The one who killed me... is among the Five Elders—' Before the words finished, subtle footsteps rang out from the darkness. Chen Ji turned sharply, only to see a familiar figure slowly walking out from the depths of the passage.

text.content: Deep within the ruins, a ghostly blue light like a spirit that had slumbered for a thousand years slowly awakened before Chen Ji's eyes. The seal—his father's remnant—now responded to his bloodline in some ancient manner. The burning sensation in his chest grew increasingly intense, as if a slumbering giant beast was awakening within him. The patterns on the seal bore a striking resemblance to the mark on Chen Ling's neck. In his hazy memories, he seemed to have seen this pattern before, on that rainy night when his father had sighed alone in the depths of night.

'Ji'er...' The aged and familiar voice came from the depths of the seal, carrying a tenderness and weariness unseen for three years. Chen Ji stood frozen, his fingertips trembling uncontrollably. He looked toward the sound, seeing a phantom figure emerge at the seal's center—his father's face, long blurred from memory. Chen Xuan now appeared before him as a remnant soul. His eyes instantly burned with酸涩, and three years of suppressed longing burst forth like a flood breaking its dam, nearly shattering all his disguises.

dialogue.content: 'Father... why are you here?' The voice was hoarse, barely recognizable as his own. Chen Ji stepped forward, only to be stopped by an invisible barrier surrounding the seal. His hand pressed against the light curtain, his palm stinging with piercing pain, yet he couldn't bear to withdraw. His father's figure was so real, yet so illusory—as if a touch would make it vanish forever.

text.content: The phantom gently raised its hand, ethereal fingertips lightly touching Chen Ji's face through the light curtain. There was no warmth, yet his heart clenched with pain. The father's image was far more aged than in memory, temples graying, brow deeply lined with the marks of time—a visage Chen Ji had never witnessed. When he was still young, his father had vanished, leaving him only his mother's parting words and a fragmented mystery.

dialogue.content: 'Father, tell me what truly happened that year? Who harmed you?' Chen Ji's voice was low and urgent, his fists clenched so tightly his fingernails cut deep into his palms. For three years, he had survived as atrash in the lowest rungs of the Tianqing Sect, countless times teetering on the edge of life and death, all for this one day—to uncover the truth. Now that his father stood before him, how could he not be shaken? Yet his hand remained steady on the Tianji Record Fragment, perceiving every trace of elemental fluctuation around him—this was a ruin, and illusory formation traps could appear at any moment.

text.content: The phantom slowly nodded, a bitter smile forming on its aged features. It opened its mouth, and fragmented words came through, each syllable seeming to be forcibly extracted from the cracks of time. The phantom gestured through the air, and a blurry scene materialized—a dark, windy night. Five figures confronted each other in a secluded place. One figure's back bore an uncanny resemblance to Chen Xuan, while the other four... Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. Though their faces were indistinct, he could never mistake that unique elemental fluctuation and their distinctive attire.

dialogue.content: 'The Five Elders... it was indeed you!' Chen Ji growled, his voice seething with overwhelming hatred. His chest heaved violently, and countless days and nights flashed through his mind—his pretense as atrash, enduring bullying, surviving in the darkest corners of the Tianqing Sect, while the true murderers were revered as pillars of justice by thousands. Killing intent surged like wild grass, nearly overwhelming his reason. But then, the ground beneath his feet flickered with a peculiar light—the illusory formation's fluctuation.

text.content: Chen Ji snapped awake, a chill shooting up his spine to the back of his skull. In three years at the Tianqing Sect, he had witnessed too many schemes and intrigues, knowing well that losing emotional control was a cultivator's most fatal weakness. Those people had been able to harm his father back then—how could they possibly fail to set up contingencies in these ruins? His fingers dug deep into his palms, the sharp pain restoring some clarity to his mind. The phantom still hovered in mid-air, its gaze carrying a profound meaning, as if saying: You've finally noticed.

'Ji'er, your father doesn't have much time left.' The phantom's voice grew increasingly faint, its form beginning to show fine cracks. 'What happened that year was exceedingly complicated. Your father can only tell you this—the one who harmed me wasn't all of them, but it was certainly one among them...' The phantom's voice abruptly stopped. An expression of resolve flashed across its aged face. 'The evidence... is right there...' It suddenly raised its hand, pointing toward a spot behind Chen Ji where an ancient jade slip faintly glowed.

Chen Ji followed the direction. The jade slip lay quietly on the stone platform, its surface carved with the same patterns as the seal. His heart raced wildly, almost bursting from his chest. Three years—he had waited for this moment for three long years. Yet his footsteps halted where they were, his gaze shifting between his father's phantom and that jade slip. The illusory formation's fluctuation persisted, and the father phantom before his eyes... was it real? Or the beginning of another trap? His hand had already quietly pressed against the Tianji Record Fragment, ready to activate its foresight at any moment.

choice.prompt: The father's phantom was right before his eyes, and the evidence lay within reach. The illusory formation's fluctuation signaled danger—you must make a choice—

choices.text: Analyze calmly and first confirm the phantom's authenticity
choices.description: Do not act rashly. Use the Tianji Record Fragment to sense the phantom's elemental fluctuation, confirming whether it is truly his father's remnant soul and not bait constructed by an illusory formation.

choices.visible_reward: Obtain key information: confirm the truth, avoid falling into a trap

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcing down the churning emotions. He did not rush toward the jade slip. Instead, he slowly closed his eyes, his palm touching the Tianji Record Fragment. The fragment's surface glowed faintly, and a thread of pure perceptive power emanated from his body, like invisible tendrils probing toward that phantom. After a moment, he opened his eyes, a hint of relief flickering within them—true blood resonance. He would never mistake his father's aura. The illusory formation's fluctuation did exist, but it wasn't targeting him; rather, it was the ruins' own protective mechanism.

choices.text: Trust your intuition and immediately obtain the jade slip
choices.description: Three years of waiting has been long enough. Whether there is a trap or not, he must obtain the evidence with his own hands. Even if it is an illusory formation, he will shatter it with his own hands.
choices.visible_cost: May trigger the illusory formation trap, falling into danger
choices.visible_reward: Obtain the evidence first, gaining the initiative
choices.risk_hint: If it is an illusory formation construction, you may fall into the enemy's preset trap

text.content: Chen Ji hesitated no longer. His form became a blur of motion as he charged toward the stone platform. His speed was immense, yet the instant before he touched the jade slip, he froze abruptly—a razor-sharp sword energy came sweeping from the side, aiming directly for his throat. The three characters 'Chen Ji' rang in his ear like frost, and Chen Ji dodged sideways, only to see a familiar figure emerge from the shadows—one of the Five Elders of the Tianqing Sect, his 'Uncle' Zhao, who had once treated him rather kindly, now regarding him with nothing but icy killing intent in his eyes.

choices.text: Dual verification, simultaneous perception and action
choices.description: While using the Tianji Record to perceive the authenticity of the phantom, he also divided some attention to guard against possible ambushes. He wouldn't give up the opportunity to obtain evidence while confirming safety.
choices.visible_cost: Distraction might cause perception to be imprecise, overlooking certain details
choices.visible_reward: Balancing safety and efficiency, demonstrating superb spiritual control
choices.risk_hint: If the enemy's strength exceeds expectations, one might be caught between defending both front and back

text.content: A cunning glint flickered in Chen Ji's eyes. As he extended his perception toward his father's phantom, his body silently approached the stone platform. The two forces were perfectly balanced within him, neither interfering with the other nor revealing his true intentions. When his perception confirmed it was genuine bloodline energy, his hand had already touched the cold surface of the jade slip—at that very moment, a fierce palm strike came from behind. Chen Ji's lips curved into a cold smile as his body twisted grotesquely, dodging the lethal blow at an angle that defied the laws of physics, while his other hand firmly grasped the jade slip.

The phantom gradually dissolved, his father's aged face becoming translucent in the light. His gaze fell upon Chen Ji, brimming with complex emotions—reluctance intertwined with quiet satisfaction. The specter opened its mouth as if to speak, yet the voice had grown so faint it was nearly inaudible. Chen Ji stared intently at his father's fading visage, an ineffable sorrow rising within him. For three years, he had endlessly imagined reuniting with his father, never anticipating it would unfold like this—within arm's reach, yet forever beyond reach.

Just as the phantom was about to completely vanish, his father's voice echoed from the abyss, crystallizing in Chen Ji's consciousness, each syllable searing into his spirit like a brand. "Ji'er... Father has wronged you... wronged Lingling... If only I had uncovered the Tianji Record's secret earlier, perhaps... cough cough..." The phantom convulsed with violent coughing, cracks spreading across its ethereal form. "The evidence... lies within the jade slip... but be vigilant... Father trusted too readily..." The voice abruptly ceased. His father's gaze shifted to something behind him, a flash of terror crossing his features.

Chen Ji spun around sharply, only to find an empty corridor stretching before him. His spiritual sense expanded outward, yet detected nothing amiss. But his father's terrified gaze chilled him to the bone—was someone there? Or something far more sinister? He turned back, desperate to hear his father's dying words, but found the phantom had nearly faded entirely, leaving only a blurry silhouette wavering in the light. His father cast one final glance at him, lips trembling, delivering words that froze his blood— "The one who killed me... resides among the Five Elders!"

choice.prompt: His father's final words struck like thunderclaps beside his ears—the Five Elders, those venerable seniors he once revered and trusted. Chen Ji's rationality and hatred clashed violently within him.

choices.text: Suppressing rage, calmly analyzing the Five Elders' movements
choices.description: Without rushing to conclusions, he first recalled the Five Elders' recent activities, analyzing who held the most suspicion and who was most likely to appear at the ruins. He would use reason to suppress hatred, avoiding startling the prey.
choices.visible_cost: This requires time to gather intelligence, potentially missing the opportunity to confront them on the spot
choices.visible_reward: Obtain a more comprehensive suspicion analysis, devise a more thorough plan
choices.risk_hint: If the murderer discovers your awareness, they may strike first

text.content: Chen Ji closed his eyes, forcefully pressing the surging rage into the deepest recesses of his heart. He silently recited the names and characteristics of the Five Elders—Sect Master Cloudclear Zhenren had been in seclusion for years, his disposition detached; Elder Zhao was affable yet perpetually absent at critical moments; Elder Sun controlled the sect's finances, entangled deepest with the outer court forces; Elder Qian specialized in artifact refinement, his nature forthright yet unsuited for intrigue; Elder Li oversaw discipline, impartial and unwavering yet因此得罪不少人... Everyone held suspicion, and everyone possessed alibis. Yet this precisely demonstrated that the events of that year had been meticulously orchestrated—no single person could have managed it alone.

choices.text: Unleashing fury, vowing blood for blood
choices.description: Three years of restraint had reached its limit. Whoever the murderer was, Chen Ji would make them pay. This rage would become his driving force for breakthrough, the finest tribute to his father.
choices.visible_cost: May lose rational judgment, be swayed by emotions
choices.visible_reward: Release long-suppressed fury, awaken the deeper potential of bloodline powers
choices.risk_hint: Fury may cloud judgment, plunging into greater peril

text.content: Chen Ji let loose a low, guttural roar toward the heavens. Three years of suppressed fury erupted like a breaching flood. His eyes blazed crimson as his spiritual energy fluctuations surged violently—that was the power from his bloodline's depths responding to his emotions. For the first time in three years, he allowed his rage to consume him fully, no longer restraining, no longer feigning. "Five Elders..." His voice dropped to a dangerous, ominous timbre, like a curse from the abyss itself. "I will teach you what it means to pay in blood!" The tyrannical energy exploded outward, shattering the stone platform beneath his feet, sending ancient dust billowing through the desolate ruins.

The moment the phantom vanished completely, the ruins fell into absolute silence. Chen Ji stood alone before the seal, clutching the jade slip still warm with residual energy, his heart churning with mixed emotions. Slowly, he extended his spiritual sense into the jade slip. Images flooded his mind—memories his father had left behind before death, a past he had never known. In the visions, his father sat alone at midnight, studying the Tianji Record fragments, his face filled with shock and dread, murmuring fragments like "So that's how it is," "They had no idea," and similar utterances.

Suddenly, the scene shifted. His father was cornered in a mountain valley. Chen Ji caught sight of five silhouettes—not their faces, but their distinctive spiritual energy fluctuations and attire were unmistakable. The five were arguing intensely, debating something. Chen Ji strained to listen, catching only fragments—"Tianji Record," "cannot let outsiders know," "must eliminate the witnesses"... Then, one of them struck suddenly! A fierce sword qi lunged directly at his father's vitals!

Chen Ji's eyes nearly burst from their sockets, but he forcibly restrained his impulses and continued observing the memory. In the vision, his father fought five opponents alone—though skilled, he was hopelessly outnumbered. Just as the fatal blow was about to land, his father suddenly activated some power within the Tianji Record. A brilliant light engulfed the entire valley, and the five men's faces became visible in that radiance. Though Chen

The memory came to an abrupt end as his father's final voice emerged from the jade slip: 'Ji'er, I knew you would find your way here. This evidence may not be enough to secure a conviction, but it will let you understand the truth. Remember, among the Five Elders, one must be the murderer, yet the other four are not necessarily innocent. The events of those years touched upon deeper secrets of the Tianji Record—your father ran out of time to investigate...' The voice paused. 'Lingling... her mark is the key... protect her well...' The words faded, and the light on the jade slip dimmed completely, leaving only the cold touch reminding Chen Ji that this was no dream.

Chen Ji gripped the jade slip tightly, his knuckles whitening from the pressure. His mind replayed his father's final moments over and over—the five figures, the heated argument, that fatal sword strike... and the guilt and reluctance in his father's eyes as he gazed at Chen Ling at the end. Lingling, the name he'd hidden in the softest corner of his heart for years, now surfaced again through his father's words. She was not merely his sister—she was the key to this entire puzzle. The mark on her neck was the key to opening some great door.

Just then, a faint tremor came from deep within the ruins. Chen Ji raised his head sharply, a flicker of wariness crossing his gaze. He quickly composed himself, tucked the jade slip into his chest, and quietly retreated. This place was not suitable for lingering—regardless of whether the illusion formation had targeted him, if his father's remnant soul could appear here, others could follow the traces. He had to leave quickly,带走这 before anyone discovered him一枚足以颠覆天青宗的证据. But just as he turned, a familiar voice came from behind—'Chen Ji? Is that you?'

That voice was cold and proud, carrying a hint of scrutiny and doubt. Chen Ji's footsteps halted, alarm bells ringing in his heart—the visitor was no other than Su Qingyao, the Inner Disciple Senior Fellow of Tianqing Sect, the woman who had repeatedly tried to approach him and find weaknesses in him. He slowly turned around, his face displaying perfectly calibrated fear and confusion, the cowardly facade flawless. But inside, his mind raced—wasn't she supposed to be at a Sect Competition? Why would she appear here? Coincidence or pursuit? How much had she seen? How much had she heard?
